newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nomura Sec's aid for unit seen positive for shares.
newsitem.headline: Nomura Sec's aid for unit seen positive for shares.

text.p: Nomura Securities Co Ltd's decision to provide aid to its troubled finance affiliate will improve the financial strength of the Nomura group and any share price dips are a good buying opportunity, analysts said on Friday.
"It was the right thing to do. It should be interpreted positively," David Threadgold, a financial analyst at BZW Securities (Japan), said.

Shares in the top Japanese broker were down 30 yen to 1,950 yen at midday on Friday, after it announced late on Thursday it would provide support to its non-bank affiliate and post a special loss of 371 billion yen in the first half of 1996/97 ending September 30.
Nomura's vice president Atsushi Saito said that the company will post a net loss in the first half as it does not plan to sell securities to help write off problem loans at the affiliate.
For the first five months, Nomura posted 59 billion yen in parent current profit, he said.

Several analysts said that Nomura's net loss would total about 300 billion yen. Noting Nomura's profit in the first five months, James Fiorillo, an analyst at ING Baring Securities, said that the firm was on track to record better than expected profits this year despite the market slump.

"Nomura seems to be following the lead of Japan's major banks which reported massive losses last fiscal year in order to resolve the 'jusen' (mortgage firm) problem. We argue, as a result, that this is good news for the firm," Fiorillo said.
Analysts said that not only Nomura but also other major brokers face the prospect of having to deal with problem loans held by their non-bank affiliates.
BZW's Threadgold said that he expects Nikko Securities Co Ltd and Daiwa Securities Co Ltd to make a similar announcement for their non-bank affiliates "not before too long".

Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd may face difficulty in helping to write off problem loans at its non-bank affiliates in the current business year as it was undermined by a summer slump in the Tokyo stock market, analysts said. But Yamaichi will show its resolve to solve the group's problems as quickly as possible, they said.

Shares in Yamaichi ended the morning down 10 yen at 683 yen. Nikko was steady at 1,170 yen, and Daiwa was down 30 yen at 1,240 yen. On Friday morning, the securities sector was the worst performing sector on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, down 1.26 percent compared with a 0.28 percent decline in the Nikkei.

Market sources said the share price falls in second-tier brokerages followed downward earnings revisions by nine brokers on Thursday, of which seven said that they would post parent current losses for the first half of 1996/97.
For the full 1996/97 year, however, almost all of the brokers expect profits.
Analysts said that it would be difficult for many of them to meet their profit forecasts as their view of market activity for the second half was too optimistic.
"Some of them must revise their forecast for 1996/97 again," one said.
